references.text: The Harvest Festival (hillulim) is connected to the laws concerning the first fruits and the harvest celebration, where the people were to rejoice before the Lord
The Feast of Tabernacles included celebration after the grape harvest, with joy and thanksgiving
Describes how joy and gladness have been taken away from the vineyards, and the treading of grapes has ceased - the same imagery as in Judges
The Lord roars from on high and raises his voice against his dwelling place; he cries out like those who tread grapes against all the inhabitants of the earth
The image of new wine in the grape cluster and blessing within it contrasts with the curse in Judges 9:27
A warning not to rejoice at the threshing floor as the nations do, for they have committed spiritual adultery away from their God - a similar context of idolatry
The people sat down to eat and drink, and rose up to play - parallel to the meal in the temple of idols
